# Objective

In Lab 5, you made cleaning decisions explicit and reproducible in a data-processing pipeline. In this lab, you will collect a small dataset from a live website, preserve the extracted records before cleaning, and compare HTML scraping with a JSON API.

You will work with the official [October 2025 General Conference index](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2025/10?lang=eng). The goal is to collect talk metadata and transcript text for one conference—not to crawl the whole website.

## Before you begin

- Work only within the designated October 2025 conference.
- Do not download a cached HTML file or use a prebuilt copy of the scraped output.
- Keep requests polite and bounded. The provided script waits between talk-page requests and does not follow links outside the conference.
- The raw file is evidence of what the scraper extracted. Do not manually edit it or silently clean text while scraping.
- A page layout can change. If your scraper returns no talks, inspect the current page and explain the problem rather than weakening checks until it appears to work.

# Part 4: Responsible and reproducible collection

## 6. Reliability and ethics

A scraper can collect publicly visible data and still be unreliable or inappropriate. Consider request load, site terms, attribution, copyright, personal information, and whether the data are necessary for the task.

**Your answer:** Identify (1) one reliability risk and (2) one ethical, legal, or reproducibility concern in this lab. For each, suggest a practical mitigation. Do not collect more pages or data than the assignment requires.
